chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to permit regarding (a dispute over) a debt: the testimony of one man and the oath of the owner of the debt. But regarding the (sighting of the) new moon, he would not permit it except with two just witnesses.

key_terms.الدَّيْن: Debt, financial obligation owed by one party to another
key_terms.الْهِلَال: The new crescent moon; its sighting determines the start of Islamic months
key_terms.شَاهِدَا عَدْل: Two just witnesses; witnesses of established moral uprightness (adala), a higher evidentiary standard
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath, sworn statement; legally binding oath in Islamic procedure

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on testimony for debt disputes versus the sighting of the new moon?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports a ruling from the Prophet (SAWW) distinguishing two evidentiary standards: for financial debt disputes, the combination of one witness plus the plaintiff's oath suffices, but for the sighting of the new crescent moon (hilal) — which determines the start of Islamic months including Ramadan — two witnesses of established just character (adala) are required. This distinction reflects the Prophet's jurisprudential legacy in setting higher communal evidentiary standards where collective religious observance is at stake.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had allowed regarding the debt, a testimony of one man and an oath of the owner of the debt, and it does not happen to be permissible regarding the (sighting of) the new moon except for two just witnesses’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, in the matter of loan accepted the testimony of one man and the oath of the creditor. However, in the case of the sighting of new moon he would only accept two witnesses.’”
